title: a record-path refusal names every way out, remove included
intention: When artifactgate refuses or names a change at a record path, its text lists every way out the door offers, `cairn artifact remove <path> --why` included, so a delete or move of a record is never a dead end that only reading the source can open.
why: Measured 2026-11-20: a refused mv of bin/validations/test_cairn_runs_from_cmd_with_no_bash.json named only write and hand-edit. The real exit, `cairn artifact remove`, was found by reading source. A refusal that hides the door it wants used invites the plaster it exists to stop.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel: an exit found by reading source is re-derived every time); Law 4 (the gate is physics; its text is the instruction the physics gives).
how: In bin/cmd/artifactgate, REFUSAL's 'The way through' gains a line for a record to delete or move away: `cairn artifact remove <path> --why '...'` (and for a move, remove then write at the new path). AFTER gains the same line beside undo and park. Nothing about what is refused changes: WRITE_VERBS, DOOR_FORMS and the record regex are untouched. A red-first proof calls verdict() on a Bash mv and an rm of a record path, and on an Edit of one, and reads AFTER, asserting `cairn artifact remove` in each.

the after-run naming text (AFTER, formatted) contains `cairn artifact remove`
what the gate refuses and allows is unchanged: bin/proofs/test_artifact_gate.py still passes, and verdict('Bash', `cairn artifact remove <record> --why x`) is still None

decisions.text: D1: REFUSAL and AFTER in artifactgate each name `cairn artifact remove <path> --why '...'` as the way out for a record to delete or move; no change to what is refused.
D2: a red-first proof, PROVES {1,2,3}, calling artifactgate's verdict() in process as test_artifact_gate.py does, one tooth per clause.
